title: III-IV. Barbarians ancient and recent; the ancient Getae and Egyptians (Herodotus, Diodorus)
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the former Herodotus bears witness in book 4; concerning the latter Diodorus Siculus in book 1 of the Library, number 93. The Egyptians judge that their parents and ancestors have stood as translated toward an eternal dwelling. The Getae do not think that they themselves cease, but that he who has died goes across toward Zamolxis. IV. The ancient, such as the Getae and the Egyptians. III. Barbarians — both the ancient and those recently and newly discovered — have acknowledged it.
pass_b_english: III. Barbarians — both the ancient and those recently and newly discovered — have acknowledged it.

IV. The ancient, such as the Getae and the Egyptians. The Getae do not think that they themselves cease, but that he who has died goes across to Zamolxis. The Egyptians judge that their parents and ancestors have been translated to an eternal dwelling. Concerning the former Herodotus bears witness in book 4; concerning the latter Diodorus Siculus in book 1 of the Library, number 93.
source_text: III. Barbari, prisci juxta & nuperi noviterque reperti agnoverunt. IV. Prisci, ut Getae & Aegyptii. Getae se non putant, sed eum, qui defunctus fuerit, meare ad Zamolxim. Aegyptii, parentes & majores suos ad aeternam habitationem translatos autumant. De illis testatur Herodotus lib. 4. de his Diodorus Siculus lib. 1. Bibliothecae num. 93.
